deep.reconstruction:
Dated 18.1.84, this is the first page of the dossier on 'systèmes de pseudo-droites'. The boxed title reads 'Les 5 variantes de la surface de déploiement d'un syst. de pseudo-droites', while the text says 'Quatre possibilités'.

Setting, inferred from this page and the next. Σ = {D_1,...,D_n} is an arrangement of pseudolines in the real projective plane. The two sphere sketches draw it on the 2-sphere, the double cover of RP^2: a yellow boundary circle, red pseudolines and black antipodal points.

A 'position relative' (p.r.) is the combinatorial type of one further pseudoline relative to Σ. The types are graded by degeneracy:
- stable: generic position;
- sous-stable: passing through one vertex of Σ;
- supersingulière: coinciding with some D_i. There are exactly n of these, which explains 'les n pos. rel. supersingulières'.

The 'graphe de déploiement' A has positions as vertices and specializations/transitions as edges. The 'surface de déploiement' X is a 2-dimensional cell complex in which vertices of A become faces. It is meant to be a combinatorial model of the space of all pseudolines relative to Σ, the analogue of the dual projective plane of a line arrangement. In modern language it is a cellular model of the one-element extension space of the rank-3 oriented matroid of Σ.

The page treats the delicate points of X: the supersingular positions.

Variant 1 (surface X_0). Supersingular positions are not allowed as vertices of A. The pseudolines near D_i then accumulate at a single 'supersingular vertex' of X_0. These n vertices are the only ones of order 4n rather than 4, so the generic vertices form a 4-valent map. The sketch shows a star of rays around s, with an antipodal pair of faces F, F' marked in red, for n = 5. The margin notes that X_0 has no 'bouts libres' at a supersingular vertex.

Variant 2 (surface X_1). Supersingular positions are admitted as vertices of A, hence as faces F of X. Direct specializations from a sous-stable position to D_i are admitted as edges; these are exceptional specialization axes. They are chosen as short as possible (combinatorial length 1) and placed equidistant between the nearest generation (transition) axes. Around the supersingular face F one then glues:
- the 2(n-1) faces of nearby sous-stable positions, along arcs of combinatorial length 1. These are pseudolines close to D_i passing through one of its vertices, on either side.
- the nearby stable faces, each lying between two consecutive sous-stable faces and touching F at one vertex.
Grothendieck corrects himself: 2(n-1) holds only when Σ is stable (simple). In general the count is 2n_i, where n_i is the number of vertices of Σ on D_i. The lower-right sketch shows F with sous-stable and stable faces attached along its boundary.

The next page continues. On X_1 all vertices, including those on the supercritical faces, are 4-valent. The 'bouts libres' (free ends) created depend on parity: n even gives 6(n-1), too many; n odd gives 2(n-1), exactly what is needed to describe (X,Σ) 'affinisé' by D_i. The proposed fix is to replace each supercritical vertex of X_0 by a small supercritical disc.

The problem served is to build a canonical combinatorial surface, presumably a combinatorial projective plane or sphere, attached to any pseudoline arrangement. It should play the role of the dual plane, with good local structure (4-valent vertices, correct gluing) at the degenerate positions.
errors: The order of a supersingular vertex in X_0 is stated as 4n. Counting nearby faces as on the rest of the page gives 2(n-1) sous-stable plus 2(n-1) stable faces, i.e. 4(n-1) (or 4n_i for non-simple Σ). Either n counts something else here (e.g. n+1 pseudolines), or 4n is a slip; the star sketch labelled n=5 cannot settle it from the image.
The count 2(n-1) is explicitly flagged by Grothendieck himself as valid only for stable Σ; in general it is 2n_i.
The title announces 5 variants, the text 'quatre possibilités', and only two are developed on this page.

ideas.what: Surface of relative positions of an extra pseudoline with respect to an arrangement Σ ('surface de déploiement'), as a combinatorial dual plane
ideas.modern_name: Extension space of a rank-3 oriented matroid / combinatorial dual of a pseudoline arrangement / topological plane extending an arrangement
ideas.usually_credited_to: Goodman–Pollack (cell complexes of arrangements, 1980s); Sturmfels–Ziegler, extension spaces of oriented matroids (1993); Goodman–Pollack–Wenger–Zamfirescu, arrangements and topological planes (1994)
ideas.where_published: unsure (possibly an allusion in Esquisse d'un programme, Jan. 1984; not verified)

ideas.what: Stratification of positions as stable / sous-stable / supersingular, with specialization arrows forming the graph A
ideas.modern_name: Face poset / covector stratification of the extension space; generic vs degenerate single-element extensions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Las Vergnas, Bland–Las Vergnas (oriented matroid extensions, 1978); Sturmfels–Ziegler

ideas.what: Alternative treatments of the degenerate positions (pseudoline = D_i): collapse to a high-valence vertex (X_0) or blow up to a face F glued to 2n_i neighbouring faces (X_1)
ideas.modern_name: Local blow-up/truncation of a cell complex at a singular vertex; vertex figure of the dual point of D_i

ideas.what: Count of neighbouring positions of D_i: 2n_i sous-stable faces (two per vertex of Σ on D_i), interleaved with stable faces
ideas.modern_name: Link of the dual point of D_i in the extension space / dual arrangement

missed.claim: In January 1984 Grothendieck was constructing, for an arbitrary (possibly non-stretchable) pseudoline arrangement, a combinatorial surface parametrizing relative positions of an extra pseudoline. This is a cellular model of the rank-3 extension space or dual topological plane. Its local structure is treated in detail at the degenerate positions (4-valence, gluing of the faces dual to the D_i). The work predates Sturmfels–Ziegler's extension spaces (1993) and the Goodman–Pollack–Wenger–Zamfirescu theorem that every arrangement lies in a topological plane (1994). It does not appear to be cited in that literature.
missed.quote: Les 5 variantes de la surface de déploiement d'un syst. de pseudo-droites
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Grothendieck's explicit cell structure on a 'dual surface' with 4-valent vertices may give a canonical cell decomposition of the rank-3 extension space or of the topological plane through an arrangement. It could be compared with existing constructions and with the extension space conjecture, which is true in rank 3 but false in general (Liu, 2020).

missed.claim: The choice among the 4–5 variants (X_0 with order-4n vertices, X_1 with supersingular faces, the small-disc modification) is left open. The parity anomaly on the next page (6(n-1) vs 2(n-1) free ends) suggests the construction is not yet canonical.
missed.quote: il y a intérêt à les choisir aussi courts que possible ... savoir de longueur combinatoire 1, et placés à égale distance entre les axes de transition
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A canonical, parity-independent combinatorial dual of a pseudoline arrangement would be a clean object in oriented-matroid theory. The difficulty Grothendieck hits may point to a genuine subtlety.

deep.surprise_reason: Grothendieck's work on pseudoline arrangements is documented only by archive listings. This page shows a concrete, technically detailed construction of a dual/extension surface roughly a decade before the comparable literature. It is a notable unpublished detail, but the page itself is a technical case analysis with no finished new theorem.
transcription_corrections: Margin NB: 'bords lisses' should almost certainly read 'bouts libres' (free ends), consistent with the next page.

'Le nombre 2(n-1) est d'ailleurs incident commun. Le cas courant, seulement dans le cas stable' likely reads something like 'Le nombre 2(n-1) est d'ailleurs inexact en général, [valable] seulement dans le cas stable; dans le cas général c'est 2n_i, où n_i est le nombre de sommets sur D_i'.
Title box: 'Les 5 variantes de la surface de déploiement d'un syst. de pseudo-droites' — the text body says 'Quatre possibilités'.
Figure legend 'F : face supersingulière [?]' probably reads 'F_i face supercritique', consistent with 'faces supercritiques' on the next page.

Margin: 'traité ... ps. rel. ... faces incidentes : c) ... de points antipodiques F, F'' probably concerns pos. rel. ... and two antipodal positions F, F' at the vertex s, matching the red antipodal pair in the star sketch.
